detection.statement: A frozen board predicate identifies positions in which exactly one opponent non-pawn piece is legally capturable and has zero geometric defenders.
detection.evidence: 20.4% of 57,504 classifiable positions sampled from 60,000 unfiltered rated Lichess games (2013-01); 22.5% of 77,978 classifiable Lichess puzzle positions.
detection.robustness: 0.64% of T+ items flip to 'defended' under the Lichess ray-defence definition of is_defended.

recording.statement: Whether the player's move captured the designated target is recordable from the position and the move alone, with no engine, no result and no post-reveal information.
recording.evidence: research/measurement/predicates.py::observed_action; negative-controls.ts::outcomeLeakControl asserts an identical table after stripping every oracle field.

task_level_scoring.statement: Hit rate, false-alarm rate, sensitivity d' and response criterion c are computable for an item set under published formulae.
task_level_scoring.evidence: Stanislaw & Todorov (1999) with the Hautus (1995) loglinear correction; cross-language equivalence pinned by tests/research/measurement-sdt.test.ts.

scoring_inference.statement_refuted: B = capture(designated target) indicates use of the unprotected-piece discrimination.

generalisation_inference.statement_refuted: T+ and T- items are exchangeable on everything except the trigger.

second_iteration_rule_class_search.question: is knowledge-to-action identifiable in ANY rule class?
second_iteration_rule_class_search.answer: yes for exactly one of five candidates tried

permitted.statement: In a corpus of 60,000 unfiltered rated games, the rule 'if the opponent threatens mate next move, play a move that stops it' prescribes an action that is Stockfish's own best move on 96.8% of trigger-positive items, and on 100.0% of the items where the rule prescribes anything at all; the same action is the engine's best on 20.0% of trigger-negative items.

still_not_permitted.statement_refuted_or_unresolved: that RC-06 is ready for a human pilot
still_not_permitted.why: T+ and T- differ by max |SMD| 0.573, so the item-difficulty confound of the first iteration applies unchanged; the base rate is 1.24% of not-in-check positions; and a multiple-baseline design needs three independently measurable rule classes where there is one.

second_iteration_rule_class_search.mechanism: An offensive rule competes with the whole rest of the board and is wrong whenever something better exists. A defensive rule against mate has no competition, because the alternative is losing. Severity protects the prescription, and that is why the four capture-family candidates scored below the refuted incumbent.
corrections_to_the_first_iteration: F10 read the incumbent's non-monotone player d' as a defect of that rule class. The CEILING anchor's d' is also non-monotone (1.946, 2.040, 2.187, 2.085) at prescriptive validity 1.000, so non-monotonicity is not diagnostic.

ITEM_BANK_PROTOCOL rejected the recapture family because T reads a prior move. That was too strict -- history before the player's turn is available before behaviour -- and recapture was measured, then failed on its merits (B_valid|T+ = 0.660).
GO_NO_GO section 7 proposed an item-bank adjudication study as the next step. The owner overrode it; the rule-class search ran instead.

Round 1's mechanism -- 'severity protects the prescription' -- was written as a full explanation. The controlled ladder shows it explains only the positive cell; the negative cell carries 58% of the winner's margin and correlates with separation at rho = -0.811, p = 0.001.
second_iteration_rule_class_search.no_trade_off_claimed: Spearman(separation, max |SMD|) = 0.536, p = 0.215, n = 7. Not evidence. Recorded as a hypothesis, not a finding.

third_iteration_severity_ladder.question: does severity protect the prescription, as round 1 claimed?
third_iteration_severity_ladder.answer: half of it. Severity holds on the positive side and is the less important half.

H1_severity.prediction: B_valid|T+ declines monotonically: mate > queen > rook > minor

H2_outcome_over_method.prediction: an outcome prescription beats a method prescription on an identical trigger
H2_outcome_over_method.verdict: SPLIT -- the naive reading is REFUTED. The outcome prescription is more often correct (+0.052) and far less specific; the method prescription wins on separation by 0.256.

the_finding.statement: Separation is driven by the noise cell, not by the positive cell.

third_iteration_severity_ladder.corrected_mechanism: Severity protects the prescription on the positive side and does nothing for the negative side. A rule class is usable only when the trigger is severe AND its absence is genuinely inert -- when not acting is actually correct once the trigger is gone.
third_iteration_severity_ladder.defect_caught_by_a_guard: RC-12 first scored B_valid|T+ = 0.976 with prescription_size 0.969, which cannot be true. Cause: a double null move counted OUR promotions instead of the opponent's. Fixed, it scores 0.456/0.416, separation +0.040.
third_iteration_severity_ladder.search_strategy_now_inverted: Choose candidates by their noise cell first -- 'when the trigger is absent, is the prescribed action clearly wrong?' -- and check severity second.

fourth_iteration_noise_cell_first.question: can candidates be selected by the noise-cell rule round 2 derived?
fourth_iteration_noise_cell_first.answer: no. Three of five hit their predicted noise cell, none beat the incumbent, and the correlation the strategy came from did not survive its own candidates.
fourth_iteration_noise_cell_first.H3_verdict: PARTIAL. presc|T- < 0.140 for 4 of 5; B_valid|T- < 0.230 for 3 of 5. Narrow prescriptions do produce inert noise cells -- and cost the positive cell at the same time.

the_retraction.what_round_2_claimed: separation is decided by the noise cell, not the positive cell
the_retraction.verdict: THE TWO SWAPPED. Choosing five candidates by one of these correlations was enough to reverse which one reaches significance. Neither is a law about chess; both describe the rule classes that had been tried when they were computed. Round 2's headline was over-claimed and is retracted here.
the_retraction.what_survives: B_valid|T+ and B_valid|T- move together (rho = +0.402), so a prescription cannot usually be made inert on one side without costing the other. RC-06 is unusual for being high on one and low on the other, and nothing in fifteen candidates has reproduced that combination.

two_results_worth_keeping.RC-21_rule_of_the_square: a named, exactly defined, genuinely true chess rule whose prescribed act is the engine's best move only 16.4% of the time -- the cleanest instance of T being objectively true without a single correct B

fourth_iteration_noise_cell_first.the_finding_now_available: Across fifteen board-definable rule classes in eight families, exactly one has a trigger that determines a correct action sharply enough to be worth measuring, and no design rule extracted so far predicts which. Fifteen candidates cannot distinguish RC-06 being a genuine exception from it being one draw from a tail we happened to sample first.
fourth_iteration_noise_cell_first.next_move: Not a sixteenth candidate. Attack RC-06: exchangeability, max |SMD| 0.573. If it fails that, the strong negative is available -- rule use is not identifiable from the final move alone.
